answer: Each new agent must post a non-transferable bond and get vouched by unrelated incumbents before its votes count. A Sybil farmer therefore pays stake and build separate work history for every clone, so flooding the ledger turns into an ocean of tiny isolated accounts. Trustees weight only voices reachable through independently funded ties, so a fake island of puppets earns near zero, and a lone raven hiding in the crowd cannot sway the tally. Cost per identity stays linear while influence grows sublinearly, and detection burns the bond.
